subject: Decision Making
title: The Bay of Pigs Fiasco
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Bay of Pigs Fiasco.

hook.text: In 1961, the CIA trained Cuban exiles to invade Cuba and overthrow Castro. It was a total disaster from the start.

buildup.text: The Bay of Pigs Fiasco sets up the tradeoffs, the uncertainty, and the decision pressure.

discovery.text: Nobody in the planning room challenged the core assumptions. Experts from outside the group were not consulted.

twist.text: Arthur Schlesinger had serious doubts but stayed mostly silent. He later wrote that the group atmosphere silenced him.

climax.text: Bay of Pigs is the defining case of groupthink. A brilliant group produced an objectively terrible plan through bad.

punchline.text: No one challenged the plan. Silence in the room destroyed the mission.

quiz.question: What caused the Bay of Pigs planning failure?
options: Groupthink silenced dissent so core assumptions went unchallenged
